rows.responsibility: QRhi media-overlay implementation for image/video/story/control/recognition composition, RGBA/YUV420/NV12/native-texture upload, device-pixel scaling, cache invalidation, draw ordering and resource teardown
rows.state_machine: renderer/device init -> pipeline/resource creation -> current frame/content upload or zero-copy binding -> ordered overlay composition -> source/theme/DPR/device invalidation -> deterministic release
rows.side_effects: Fabushi keeps a single canonical MediaViewer. Chromium/Electron owns decoded-frame GPU composition and platform texture lifetime; the renderer surface still releases stale media, preserves control/input ownership and survives source/fullscreen/display changes without a second Telegram renderer.
rows.failure_cases: stale frame/texture after source or device-factor change; unsupported/native frame binding failure; YUV/NV12 conversion divergence; resource leak on renderer/device teardown; recognition/control overlay drift
rows.ui_disposition: Reuse canonical MediaViewer and canonical controls. Qt QRhi shaders/textures are replaced by Chromium/Electron media/compositor surfaces; no Telegram-named renderer/component is introduced.
rows.fabushi_target: PARTIAL IMPLEMENTATION: canonical MediaViewer exposes Chromium native video playback controls, defers video pointer/wheel ownership to the media element, pauses outgoing video on source replacement/unmount and preserves fullscreen Escape behavior. Low-level QRhi/YUV/native-texture work is platform-replaced by Chromium/Electron; recognition/story/group-call rendering responsibilities remain mapped-open until later source owners and exact-head runtime evidence are closed.
rows.platform_differences: Telegram directly owns QRhi resources, shaders, YUV/NV12 textures and macOS native texture cache. Fabushi delegates those low-level responsibilities to Chromium/Electron while retaining application-level lifecycle, a11y, keyboard, error and source-replacement contracts in the one canonical MediaViewer.
